bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the salary you need to be rich in Australia

When you hear people talk about the **salary you need to be rich in Australia**, it often comes down to converting an hourly rate into an annual figure. Whether you are negotiating a job offer, planning your budget, or just curious, the basic formula is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks in a year. For a full-time employee, the standard week is 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. So if you earn $40 per hour, your annual gross pay is $40 × 38 × 52 = $79,040.

But that is only the starting point. Your actual take-home pay depends on tax, the Medicare levy, and superannuation. And the definition of ‘rich’ varies – some use the top tax bracket, others look at average weekly earnings. Let’s break it down.

## How to calculate annual pay from an hourly rate

The formula is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. We assume 38 hours per week for full-time work, but you can adjust if you work part-time or overtime. For casual employees, the rate often includes a 25% loading on top of the base award rate. For example, the national minimum wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for permanent employees, or $33.05 per hour for casuals including the loading ().

A fortnightly figure is simply the weekly amount multiplied by two. This can help when comparing salary packages that are paid fortnightly. For instance, $26.44 per hour for 38 hours gives $1,004.90 per week, or $2,009.80 per fortnight.

## National minimum wage vs award rates

The national minimum wage ($26.44 per hour) applies to employees not covered by an award or enterprise agreement. However, most workers are covered by an industry or occupation award, which sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Commission publishes the national minimum wage order each year (), while the Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award. For example, the Health Services Award changed from 1 October 2026, and the SCHADS Award will increase for home care disability employees from 1 December 2026.

If you are casual, you are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base award rate. This is not an extra you add yourself – it is built into the casual rate shown in pay guides. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains more.

## Tax and the Medicare levy on your annual salary

Once you have your annual gross figure, tax is deducted using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on the excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on the excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on the excess over $135,000
- $190,001 and above: 45% on the excess over $190,000

In addition, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. Low-income earners may qualify for a reduction (based on 2025–26 thresholds). For a single person earning $79,040, the tax would be approximately $15,138 plus $1,581 Medicare levy, leaving a take-home of about $62,321. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for your exact situation.

## Superannuation is paid on top

Employers must pay super guarantee of 12% of your ordinary earnings, on top of your salary. This does not reduce your take-home pay – it is an additional contribution to your super fund. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year, so super stops accruing on earnings above that. For a $79,040 salary, your employer adds $9,484.80 to super annually. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more.

## What does ‘rich’ mean in Australia?

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports average weekly earnings for full-time adult ordinary time as $2,083.70 per week (May 2026), which is about $108,352 annually. All employees (including part-time) average $1,579.20 per week or $82,118 annually. To be in the top tax bracket, you need over $190,000. But the **salary you need to be rich in Australia** is subjective – some aim for $250,000, others for $500,000. Our [reference tables](/data) show how different hourly rates translate to annual figures at various thresholds.

## Important notes and limitations

This guide uses the standard 38-hour week. If you work different hours, adjust accordingly. The calculations assume no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. Tax estimates use the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare reductions are based on 2025–26 single thresholds as the 2026–27 reductions were not confirmed. HELP loans, Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not included. Always check with the Australian Taxation Office for your personal situation.

For a quick conversion, use our [the timesheet](/) tool: enter your base hourly rate, tick the casual loading checkbox if applicable, and see your annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures with tax and super estimates.
